## Observed failure

Release [PR #170](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ts-starter/pull/170), package version `2026.10.28`, immutable head `eb469252ea295183d5e224a06a2e0d4b825f759c`, has a failed [test (26) job 122746026162](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ts-starter/actions/runs/40667564912/job/122746026162).

Hosted environment: Ubuntu 26.04.1, runner image `20261012.163.1`, Node `v26.12.1`, npm `11.20.0`, Bun `1.4.4+38afee6c8`. The job installs with `npm ci`, runs the npm release-check path, then `bun run release:check`. The latter invokes `bun run coverage`, whose command is `bun run build && bun run build:test && node scripts/coverage-gate.ts`: this is Node coverage under Bun script orchestration, not evidence that Bun itself caused the failure.

Both test executions report **370 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 0 cancelled**. The first execution emits its coverage report. At `2026-10-28T10:24:13Z`, the second reports:

```text
Warning: Could not report code coverage. Error [ERR_OPERATION_FAILED]:
Operation failed: coverage file is empty: <temporary coverage directory>/<coverage file>.json
```

`coverage` and `release:check` then exit 1. The second path therefore supplies no successful coverage report; later chained audit/pack/changelog/attestation checks must not be counted as executed on that path. Passing functional tests are not coverage or whole-release certification. Node 22 and CodeQL succeeded; the exact-head Node 26 failure remained current in the 10:44 UTC all-status check refresh, with no superseding attempt found.

## Expected / impact

The release gate should either produce a trustworthy complete coverage result or fail closed with actionable collector diagnostics. The observed failure correctly blocks qualification but leaves coverage collection unresolved despite passing tests. Its root cause, reproducibility and whether it is transient are unknown. This is a hosted CI observation, not a locally reproduced defect or a demonstrated application regression.

Related accepted certification context: [pm-ts-starter-n4ee at this exact head](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ts-starter/blob/eb469252ea295183d5e224a06a2e0d4b825f759c/.agents/pm/chores/pm-ts-starter-n4ee.toon). Its independent statement-metric, authored-source-scope and substantive-review requirements remain separate; this report does not claim to fulfill them or assign their tracker ID to this failure.

## Acceptance / regression criteria

- Diagnose the empty artifact using sanitized collector/subprocess completion evidence and requalify the affected Node 26 npm/Bun paths on a recorded immutable revision; retain runtime versions and complete coverage receipts.
- Preserve fail-closed behavior, required metrics and authored-source inventory. Do not silently discard empty artifacts, reduce coverage scope/thresholds or treat 370 passing tests as certification.
- Add a focused empty/truncated coverage-artifact regression around the relevant collection boundary, verifying an actionable failure without false success; if an upstream/runtime cause is established, record that evidence and an appropriate bounded regression or compatibility check.
- Confirm ordinary complete coverage still succeeds and the relevant release-check chain finishes after remediation. Record any remaining certification gaps separately.

## Duplicate check / limits

All 170 all-status issue/PR records and PR #170 conversation were checked, followed by PR #170 reviews and inline comments at 10:47 UTC: one generic approval, no inline comments and no exact coverage-artifact owner found. [#169](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-ts-starter/issues/169) concerns SDK-upgrade startup assertions on #168, unlike these passing tests. No local source execution, workflow rerun or security reproduction was performed for this report.
